lit: they can be counted by bending one's fingers

use.how: Predicate or attributive about how few there are of a group, often notable ones: 这样的专家屈指可数。屈指可数的几家医院

near.diff: 寥寥无几 stresses disappointing emptiness (hardly anyone came); 屈指可数 says the few can be named one by one, often because they stand out.

cue: You want to say that in the whole country you could name the top violin makers on your two hands.

ctx.s: 这个小镇上的饭馆{屈指可数}，大家都很熟悉。
ctx.en: There are only a handful of restaurants in this little town, and everyone knows them all.

ctx.s: 全国能做这种手术的医生{屈指可数}。
ctx.en: Only a handful of doctors in the whole country can perform this operation.

ctx.s: 他是我们公司{屈指可数}的几位技术骨干之一。
ctx.en: He is one of the few key technical experts in our company.

ctx.s: 那个年代，全村考上大学的人{屈指可数}，他就是其中之一。
ctx.en: In those days only a handful of people in the whole village got into university, and he was one of them.

ctx.s: “这家店开了多少年了？”“本地比它老的店{屈指可数}。”
ctx.en: "How long has this shop been open?" "There are only a handful of shops around here older than it."

ctx.s: 在中国足球史上，能在欧洲顶级联赛站稳脚跟的球员{屈指可数}。
ctx.en: In the history of Chinese football, the players who established themselves in Europe's top leagues are very few.

bad.s: 他{屈指可数}了一下，发现还差三天。
bad.en: (meant: he counted on his fingers and found three days were left)
bad.why: It is a fixed description meaning 'very few', not a verb for counting on one's fingers; say you counted with your fingers instead.

bad.s: 商场里的顾客{屈指可数}，挤得走不动。
bad.en: (meant: the mall was packed with countless shoppers)
bad.why: It means there are very few; it cannot describe a crowd too large to count.

use.how: Predicate about goods, tickets, housing, skilled workers in a market: 新款手机供不应求。 Also 出现供不应求的局面.

cue: A bakery's new pastry sells out every morning within an hour, and the shop simply cannot bake enough of it.

ctx.s: 这款新手机一上市就{供不应求}。
ctx.en: As soon as this new phone came out, demand outstripped supply.

ctx.s: 春节前的火车票总是{供不应求}。
ctx.en: Train tickets before the Spring Festival are always in short supply.

ctx.s: “怎么又卖完了？”“这种蛋糕太受欢迎，天天{供不应求}。”
ctx.en: "Sold out again?" "This cake is so popular that we can never make enough."

ctx.s: 由于护士{供不应求}，很多医院不得不提高工资。
ctx.en: Because there are not enough nurses to meet demand, many hospitals have had to raise pay.

ctx.s: 一线城市的学区房长期{供不应求}，价格一路上涨。
ctx.en: In the biggest cities, flats near good schools have long been in short supply, and prices keep rising.

ctx.s: 今年苹果减产，市场上出现了{供不应求}的局面。
ctx.en: The apple harvest was poor this year, so the market saw demand exceed supply.

bad.s: 仓库里堆满了卖不出去的货，真是{供不应求}。
bad.en: (meant: there is far more stock than buyers)
bad.why: It means supply falls short of demand; an unsold surplus is the opposite situation (gōng guò yú qiú).

bad.s: 这家工厂{供不应求}客户的订单。
bad.en: (meant: this factory cannot keep up with its customers' orders)
bad.why: It is a complete predicate and takes no object; say the factory's products are in short supply, or that it cannot meet the orders.

mean: far too little to solve the problem
lit: a cup of water on a cartload of burning firewood

story.text: Mencius argued that humaneness overcomes its opposite as water overcomes fire. But, he said, people who practise humaneness today are like someone throwing one cup of water on a whole cartload of firewood that is burning; when the fire does not go out, they conclude that water cannot beat fire.

use.how: Predicate, often after 只是 or 无异于, about money, aid or effort far smaller than a need: 这点钱对他来说只是杯水车薪。

near.diff: 九牛一毛 says an amount is tiny compared with what someone has; 杯水车薪 says it is tiny compared with what a problem needs.
无济于事 says something does not help at all, for any reason; 杯水车薪 says it helps a little but is far too small.

cue: A family owes huge hospital bills, and a neighbour hands over a small envelope of cash; it is kind, but nowhere near enough.

ctx.s: 他欠了那么多债，这点钱只是{杯水车薪}。
ctx.en: He owes so much that this bit of money is only a drop in the ocean.

ctx.s: 两台水泵对这么大的洪水来说简直是{杯水车薪}。
ctx.en: Against a flood this big, two pumps are hopelessly inadequate.

ctx.s: “每月加两百块工资有用吗？”“房租涨了那么多，{杯水车薪}啊。”
ctx.en: "Does a two-hundred-yuan raise help?" "With rent up that much, it barely scratches the surface."

ctx.s: 政府的补贴虽然及时，但对受灾地区来说仍是{杯水车薪}。
ctx.en: The government subsidy came quickly, but for the disaster area it is still far too little.

ctx.s: 靠几个志愿者清理整条河的垃圾，无异于{杯水车薪}。
ctx.en: Relying on a few volunteers to clear the rubbish from the whole river is a hopeless drop in the bucket.

ctx.s: 面对巨大的资金缺口，这笔捐款只能算{杯水车薪}，问题还得从根本上解决。
ctx.en: Faced with a huge funding gap, this donation is only a drop in the bucket; the problem needs a fundamental solution.

bad.s: 你送的礼物虽然{杯水车薪}，但我很感动。
bad.en: (meant: your gift was small, but it touched me)
bad.why: It describes help hopelessly short of a need, so it belittles a gift; it does not mean 'modest but kind'.

bad.s: 他的房间很小，只有{杯水车薪}。
bad.en: (meant: his room is tiny)
bad.why: It is not a general word for 'small'; it only measures help or resources against a large problem.

mean: a dazzling array of fine things on display

use.how: Predicate about goods, books, artworks or dishes on display: 货架上的商品琳琅满目。 Also attributive: 琳琅满目的展品. Not used of people.

near.diff: 应有尽有 says nothing is missing from the range; 琳琅满目 describes the eye-catching sight of many fine things laid out.
五花八门 is any wide, even confusing, variety (methods, excuses); 琳琅满目 is a pleasing display of attractive objects.

cue: You walk into a jewellery and craft fair where every stall glitters with beautiful things laid out to admire.

ctx.s: 超市的货架上{琳琅满目}，什么都有。
ctx.en: The supermarket shelves are crammed with all kinds of goods; they have everything.

ctx.s: 夜市上摆满了{琳琅满目}的小吃和工艺品。
ctx.en: The night market is filled with a dazzling array of snacks and handicrafts.

ctx.s: 走进书店，{琳琅满目}的新书让她不知道先看哪本。
ctx.en: Walking into the bookshop, she faced so many fine new books that she didn't know which to look at first.

ctx.s: “展览怎么样？”“展品{琳琅满目}，一天都看不完。”
ctx.en: "How was the exhibition?" "There was such a wealth of exhibits that you couldn't see it all in a day."

ctx.s: 春节前，商店的橱窗里{琳琅满目}，到处是年货。
ctx.en: Before the Spring Festival, shop windows are full of eye-catching New Year goods.

ctx.s: 博物馆的这个展厅里{琳琅满目}，陈列着历代精美的瓷器。
ctx.en: This museum hall is a feast for the eyes, displaying exquisite porcelain from every dynasty.

bad.s: 广场上的游客{琳琅满目}，非常热闹。
bad.en: (meant: the square was full of tourists)
bad.why: It describes fine objects on display, never people; a crowd needs a different expression.

bad.s: 他的作业里错误{琳琅满目}。
bad.en: (meant: his homework was full of mistakes)
bad.why: It is praise for a beautiful display; it cannot describe a pile of mistakes.

lit: of every shape and every colour

use.how: Mostly attributive before a plural noun: 形形色色的人、形形色色的问题. Says a group contains many different kinds; not used of one thing.

near.diff: 五花八门 often hints the variety is odd or bewildering (tricks, excuses); 形形色色 neutrally says there are many kinds, especially of people.

cue: A taxi driver says that in twenty years on the road he has carried every kind of passenger you can imagine.

ctx.s: 做出租车司机，每天都会遇到{形形色色}的人。
ctx.en: As a taxi driver, you meet all sorts of people every day.

ctx.s: 火车站里来来往往的都是{形形色色}的旅客。
ctx.en: The people coming and going in the station are travellers of every kind.

ctx.s: “当记者累吗？”“累，但能接触到{形形色色}的人和事。”
ctx.en: "Is being a reporter tiring?" "Yes, but you get to meet all kinds of people and situations."

ctx.s: 城市里生活着{形形色色}的人，每个人都有自己的故事。
ctx.en: All kinds of people live in the city, and each has a story of their own.

ctx.s: 这部小说描写了旧上海{形形色色}的人物。
ctx.en: This novel portrays the many different characters of old Shanghai.

ctx.s: 节目请来了{形形色色}的嘉宾，有农民，有科学家，也有明星。
ctx.en: The show invited all sorts of guests: farmers, scientists and celebrities.

bad.s: 她今天穿了一件{形形色色}的裙子。
bad.en: (meant: she wore a colourful dress)
bad.why: It means many different kinds within a group, not 'colourful'; one bright dress is wǔ yán liù sè.

bad.s: 这里的人非常{形形色色}。
bad.en: (meant: the people here are very diverse)
bad.why: It cannot take a degree adverb like hěn or fēicháng; say there are all sorts of people here instead.

lit: each has its thousand autumns (its own lasting worth)

use.how: Predicate after two or more people or things being compared: 这两家店各有千秋。 Says each is good in a different way, so no clear winner.

near.diff: 不相上下 says two are about equal on the same measure; 各有千秋 says each is strong in its own, different way.

cue: A friend asks which of two cities is better to live in; one has the food, the other the scenery, and you refuse to pick.

ctx.s: 这两家火锅店{各有千秋}，一家汤底香，一家肉新鲜，我都喜欢。
ctx.en: The two hotpot places each have their own strengths: one has a fragrant broth, the other fresh meat. I like them both.

ctx.s: “你觉得北京好还是上海好？”“{各有千秋}吧，很难比较。”
ctx.en: "Which do you think is better, Beijing or Shanghai?" "Each has its own appeal; it's hard to compare."

ctx.s: 三位歌手风格不同，{各有千秋}，评委很难打分。
ctx.en: The three singers have different styles and each has merits, so the judges found it hard to score them.

ctx.s: 中西医{各有千秋}，不必非要分个高低。
ctx.en: Chinese and Western medicine each have their strengths; there is no need to rank one above the other.

ctx.s: 这几款车在价格和性能上{各有千秋}，就看你更看重什么了。
ctx.en: These cars each have advantages in price or performance; it depends on what matters more to you.

ctx.s: 两位作家的作品{各有千秋}：一位擅长写人物，一位擅长写景。
ctx.en: The two writers each excel in their own way: one at character, the other at landscape.

bad.s: 这部电影{各有千秋}，非常精彩。
bad.en: (meant: this film is excellent)
bad.why: It compares two or more things that are each good; it cannot describe a single film.

bad.s: 这两个方案都很糟糕，真是{各有千秋}。
bad.en: (meant: both plans are equally bad)
bad.why: It is praise: each has real merits. Things that are equally bad are bàn jīn bā liǎng.

mean: to put on a par (usually: cannot be)
lit: to raise two things together and discuss them side by side

use.how: Almost always negated or in a rhetorical question: A和B不能相提并论。 怎么能把A和B相提并论？ Takes no object; the two things go before it.

cue: Someone compares a neighbourhood five-a-side kickabout with the World Cup final, and you object that the two are not in the same league.

ctx.s: 小区的足球赛怎么能和世界杯{相提并论}？
ctx.en: How can a neighbourhood football match be compared with the World Cup?

ctx.s: 我的厨艺和专业厨师根本不能{相提并论}。
ctx.en: My cooking is nowhere near a professional chef's; the two can't be compared.

ctx.s: “你们俩都是老师，差不多吧？”“我刚入职，哪能和他{相提并论}。”
ctx.en: "You're both teachers, so you're about the same, right?" "I've just started; I can't be mentioned in the same breath as him."

ctx.s: 意外失误和故意违规性质不同，不应{相提并论}。
ctx.en: An accidental mistake and a deliberate violation are different in nature and should not be treated as equal.

ctx.s: 有人把这部网剧和经典名著{相提并论}，我觉得太夸张了。
ctx.en: Some people put this web series on a par with the classics, which I think is going too far.

ctx.s: 今天的交通条件和三十年前已不可{相提并论}。
ctx.en: Transport today simply cannot be compared with what it was thirty years ago.

bad.s: 老师把我们两个人的作文{相提并论}了一下，说都写得很好。
bad.en: (meant: the teacher compared our two essays and said both were good)
bad.why: It is not a neutral verb 'to compare'; it is used to deny that two things are on a par.

bad.s: 我们{相提并论}这两个问题吧。
bad.en: (meant: let's discuss these two problems together)
bad.why: It takes no object and does not mean 'discuss together'; the two things must come before it.

lit: each assists the other and each completes the other

use.how: Predicate after two abstract things: 理论和实践是相辅相成的。 Also 相辅相成的关系. Used of factors, qualities or activities, rarely of people doing a task.

near.diff: 息息相关 only says two things are closely tied; 相辅相成 says each actively strengthens the other.

cue: A coach explains that reading builds a child's vocabulary, and a bigger vocabulary in turn makes reading easier and more fun.

ctx.s: 读书和写作是{相辅相成}的。
ctx.en: Reading and writing reinforce each other.

ctx.s: 在学习语言时，听和说{相辅相成}，缺一不可。
ctx.en: In language learning, listening and speaking complement each other; you need both.

ctx.s: “休息不会耽误训练吗？”“不会，休息和训练是{相辅相成}的。”
ctx.en: "Won't resting hold back my training?" "No, rest and training go hand in hand."

ctx.s: 经济发展与环境保护并不矛盾，而是可以{相辅相成}。
ctx.en: Economic growth and environmental protection are not in conflict; they can reinforce each other.

ctx.s: 这家公司的设计和技术{相辅相成}，产品才这么受欢迎。
ctx.en: The company's design and technology strengthen each other, which is why its products are so popular.

ctx.s: 理论指导实践，实践检验理论，两者形成了{相辅相成}的关系。
ctx.en: Theory guides practice and practice tests theory; the two form a mutually reinforcing relationship.

bad.s: 搬家那天，几个朋友{相辅相成}，很快就搬完了。
bad.en: (meant: my friends helped one another and finished the move quickly)
bad.why: It is about two abstract factors strengthening each other, not people pitching in on a job.

bad.s: 他们俩的意见完全相反，真是{相辅相成}。
bad.en: (meant: their views are completely opposite)
bad.why: It means the two support each other, so it cannot describe completely opposite views.

mean: closely bound up with each other

use.how: Predicate in the pattern A与B息息相关 or A和B息息相关, about issues that directly affect people's lives or each other: 物价与百姓生活息息相关。

near.diff: 唇亡齿寒 warns that if one falls the other is endangered; 息息相关 just says the two are closely connected.
相辅相成 says two things strengthen each other; 息息相关 only says they are closely connected, in either direction.

cue: A news anchor introduces a report on food prices by stressing how directly they touch every household's daily life.

ctx.s: 天气和农民的收入{息息相关}。
ctx.en: The weather is closely tied to farmers' incomes.

ctx.s: 房价的变化与每个家庭都{息息相关}。
ctx.en: Changes in house prices closely affect every family.

ctx.s: “为什么要关心环境问题？”“因为它和我们的健康{息息相关}啊。”
ctx.en: "Why should we care about the environment?" "Because it's closely bound up with our health."

ctx.s: 一个城市的发展，和交通是否方便{息息相关}。
ctx.en: A city's development is closely linked to how convenient its transport is.

ctx.s: 这次改革涉及的都是与老百姓生活{息息相关}的问题。
ctx.en: This reform deals with issues that directly concern ordinary people's lives.

ctx.s: 睡眠质量与情绪状态{息息相关}，长期失眠容易让人焦虑。
ctx.en: Sleep quality is closely bound up with mood; long-term insomnia easily makes people anxious.

bad.s: 我和小王{息息相关}，每天一起吃午饭。
bad.en: (meant: Xiao Wang and I are close friends)
bad.why: It links issues or factors that affect each other, not two friends who are close.

bad.s: 这两幅画的风格{息息相关}，看起来差不多。
bad.en: (meant: the two paintings look very similar)
bad.why: It means closely connected in effect, not similar in appearance.

lit: follow the line of reason and the writing takes shape

use.how: Predicate or adverbial (顺理成章地) about a result that follows logically from what came before: 他顺理成章地当上了队长。

near.diff: 水到渠成 says success arrives once conditions have ripened over time; 顺理成章 says a step follows logically from what came before.
理所当然 says something is only right or to be expected, often taken for granted; 顺理成章 stresses the logical sequence leading to it.

cue: A deputy manager has run the team well for years, so when the manager retires, the promotion follows quite logically.

ctx.s: 他成绩最好，{顺理成章}地拿到了奖学金。
ctx.en: He had the best grades, so it followed naturally that he got the scholarship.

ctx.s: 既然双方都同意了这个方案，下一步签合同就{顺理成章}了。
ctx.en: Since both sides have agreed to the plan, signing the contract is the logical next step.

ctx.s: 他在中国生活了十年，又会说中文，{顺理成章}地成了公司中国区的负责人。
ctx.en: He had lived in China for ten years and spoke Chinese, so it followed naturally that he became head of the company's China office.

ctx.s: “你怎么就当上班长了？”“原来的班长转学了，我是副班长，接班也就{顺理成章}了。”
ctx.en: "How did you become class monitor?" "The old monitor changed schools and I was the deputy, so taking over followed naturally."

ctx.s: 从这些数据出发，得出这个结论是{顺理成章}的。
ctx.en: Starting from these data, reaching this conclusion follows logically.

ctx.s: 公司在国内站稳脚跟后，{顺理成章}地开始开拓海外市场。
ctx.en: Once the company was firmly established at home, it moved on, as a natural next step, to markets abroad.

bad.s: 昨天他突然中了彩票，真是{顺理成章}。
bad.en: (meant: he won the lottery yesterday, amazing)
bad.why: It describes a result that follows logically from what came before; pure luck follows from nothing.

bad.s: 这次旅行一路{顺理成章}，没遇到任何麻烦。
bad.en: (meant: the trip went smoothly with no trouble)
bad.why: It is about logical consequence, not a smooth, trouble-free journey; that is yí lù shùn lì.
